summary:
Recovered authoritative context without modifying files or running the verifier-owned check.

Authority summary:
- Project authority: data/workbench/projects.json:1-584 defines the canonical registry and cargo-backed `test` check (`cargo test -p arda-core`) for the root Arda contracts. The registry currently includes root-workspace proof contracts, two disposable autonomous-acceptance projects, two bounded Rust projects, and two reviewed read-only documentation projects. This is configured project authority, not proof that those projects have executed together under one objective.
- Program authority: docs/plans/ARDA_WHOLE_SYSTEM_COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md:17-47 defines the canonical observe/retrieve/frame/decompose/authorize/schedule/place/execute/verify/review/continue loop; lines 49-98 order autonomous completion before provider routing, project fabric, daily improvement, assimilation, and whole-system acceptance.
- Autonomous-loop authority: docs/plans/AUTONOMOUS_TASK_COMPLETION_LOOP.md:23-37 says the core implementation and one bounded installed objective exist, but Hermes control, deferred/recurring restart continuation, real multi-project execution, Vairë context use, and operator acceptance remain incomplete.
- Current detailed plan: docs/plans/autonomous-task-completion/README.md:25-37 classifies queue/schedule/continuation, the full run graph, retry/revision/replan, checkpoints, verifier/critic contracts, and objective projection as source/package verified. It records bounded installed proofs, installed critic rejection and correction, and terminal outcome binding, while explicitly leaving genuine messaging-platform control, deferred/recurring wake, reviewed real-project joined close, Vairë context-use, and the operator verdict open.
- Status evidence: ARDA_SYSTEM_STATUS_REPORT.md:36-55 describes a substantial internal 0.9 kernel but incomplete autonomous completion, connected projects, Soterion retrieval, and daily improvement. Its live-runtime statements at lines 91-106 are a dated 2026-08-25 snapshot, not contemporaneous deployed proof. Some counts and maturity claims are stale relative to the 2026-08-30 plans and current registry.
- Receipt context: core/projects/tasks/queue.jsonl:46895 records this read-only recovery leaf, its approval, bounded budget, required source evidence, and acceptance criteria. Lines 46696-46894 repeatedly contain pending execute/verify records for the same disposable acceptance objective, indicating unresolved duplicate fan-out or projection/enqueue behavior in canonical queue history.

Capability classification:
- Implemented capability: source/package contracts for canonical queue and schedules, run graphs, continuation decisions, restart checkpoints, verifier/critic roles, and operator projection are recorded as implemented and tested by the active autonomous-completion program.
- Configured runtime: an installed Hermes loopback bridge/control path, scheduler/timer path, provider-backed execution path, and registered project contracts are recorded as configured. Configuration alone does not prove current health or end-to-end acceptance.
- Live deployed proof: the active plans record bounded installed timer/restart/correction closure, provider-backed critic rejection followed by revision, disposable-project provider overlap, and terminal outcome binding. No live service or endpoint was probed in this read-only file inspection; genuine messaging-platform control, same-objective deferred/recurring wake, reviewed real-project joined close, live Vairë context-use, and operator burden reduction remain unproven.

Prioritized repair backlog:
1. P0 — Stop duplicate canonical fan-out. Human-visible behavior: one objective exposes exactly one eligible next action and never accumulates repeated execute/verify pairs. Source evidence: core/projects/tasks/queue.jsonl:46696-46894 repeatedly records pending pairs for one objective. Smallest authoritative repair surface: the existing Aulë/CEO enqueue and canonical scheduler idempotency boundary keyed by objective, leaf, continuation sequence, and attempt; do not create another queue or edit generated projections.
2. P0 — Close genuine Hermes objective control. Human-visible behavior: the operator can inspect, pause, resume, reprioritize, revise, approve, reject, and cancel the same objective conversationally without handling IDs. Source evidence: docs/plans/autonomous-task-completion/01-hermes-objective-control.md:14-20 and 37-55 records loopback acceptance but leaves a real messaging-platform receipt open. Smallest authoritative repair surface: the existing Hermes-facing OperatorProjection consumer and Aulë mutation owner, with read-after-write canonical projection and one command receipt.
3. P0 — Prove deferred or recurring continuation across restart. Human-visible behavior: deferred work wakes once, survives restart and a forced failure, corrects itself within budget, and closes without another instruction. Source evidence: docs/plans/autonomous-task-completion/02-installed-scheduling-restart.md:14-33 leaves one same-objective deferred/recurring wake open. Smallest authoritative repair surface: canonical schedules.jsonl records plus the existing installed timer and continuation engine; add no parallel scheduler.
4. P0 — Execute one shared objective across reviewed real projects. Human-visible behavior: one objective safely coordinates two truthful project contracts and reaches one joined close while preserving unrelated dirty work. Source evidence: docs/plans/autonomous-task-completion/README.md:36 and 66-78 leaves reviewed real projects and joined close open; data/workbench/projects.json:326-446 provides two bounded Rust project contracts, while lines 448-582 provide reviewed read-only contracts. Smallest authoritative repair surface: existing project registry contracts, Workbench project adapter, dependency-aware run graph, and joined objective closure.
5. P1 — Bind live Vairë context use and obtain operator acceptance. Human-visible behavior: a resumed objective explains where work stopped, what context influenced the next action, and closes only when the operator confirms reduced management burden. Source evidence: docs/plans/autonomous-task-completion/README.md:37 and 64-78; ARDA_SYSTEM_STATUS_REPORT.md:119-131. Smallest authoritative repair surface: existing Vairë context/outcome receipts and canonical operator projection consumed by Hermes; do not introduce transcript or UI authority.
6. P1 — Reconcile status truth automatically. Human-visible behavior: status surfaces distinguish implemented, configured, recorded installed proof, currently live, and operator-accepted states without stale registry counts. Source evidence: ARDA_SYSTEM_STATUS_REPORT.md:31-55 and 91-106 conflicts in age and scope with data/workbench/projects.json and the 2026-08-30 autonomous plans. Smallest authoritative repair surface: a read-only reconciliation over existing project, run, schedule, service, and receipt authorities; generated projections remain consumers only.

Downstream stop conditions remain those in docs/plans/ARDA_WHOLE_SYSTEM_COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md:99-108: dirty repositories stay read-only until ownership is understood, canonical authorities must not be duplicated, and consequential external actions remain explicitly gated. The declared `cargo test -p arda-core` check was intentionally not run because independent verification owns it.
